items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: Trent's people would take care of the band... Peanuts Van Lan became ill there

ctx.x: And we entered into 19-- that was 1931. Because we had opened in Cleveland New Year's eve, 1930, which through us into 1931. In 1931, we played Oklahoma, we played parts of Arkansas, which was Alphonso Trent's home, so that gave us the base, we could loaf there, lay off there, because Trent's people would take care of the band. We played dances in Little Rock, just couldn't make any money.

There -- it was a tough scuffle. Things was just rough. Everybody kept thinking it would be better next week or next month or the next few months, but it just kept getting worse and worse, so we finally realized that we were in the grip of a deep depression and that was it. By Oliver left the band. We went to Okmulgee, Oklahoma and we played around Holland Okmulgee awhile. Peanuts Van Lan became ill there and he was incoherent -- you could talk to him and nothing would happen and he couldn't understand you and…

We played through Oklahoma, we even played church concerts. To no avail. And things were really tough. We played towns like Seminole. Many small towns. It was just rough. So we changed booking agents and I can't think of the booking agent we secured, but he decided to book us into Dallas and to play some dates at the countryclubs and what-not and this we did. So we left -- we had left Oklahoma and we had gone to Arkansas and played around through Missouri and different places and we went through Kansas City on…
